speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, let me set out the proposal to allow approved financial institutions to use their security interests in residential property loans involving HDB flats as security to access liquidity from the MAS.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Like other central banks around the world, MAS lends to banks against good collateral, if the need arises, to tide them through short-term liquidity needs or times of financial market volatility.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Timely and ample liquidity provision by MAS can pre-empt and mitigate liquidity strains in banks, reducing the likelihood of spill-overs to the broader economy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: On 28 September 2020, MAS launched a Singapore Dollar Term Facility to provide banks an additional channel to borrow Singapore dollar funds at longer tenors with more forms of collateral.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MAS is introducing this Facility pre-emptively, in light of current economic headwinds, to provide greater certainty of access to central bank liquidity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will help to contain any liquidity strains before they pose a serious challenge.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MAS intends to accept the security interests in residential property loans, for both private property and public housing, as security to enhance the banks' access to MAS' SGD lending facilities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While banks in Singapore are well capitalised and maintain healthy liquidity buffers, greater and more certain access to MAS liquidity will strengthen their resilience to any future financial market stresses.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Strong and stable banks are in a better position to support the financing needs of individuals and businesses here in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The acceptance of security interests in residential property loans as security for central bank liquidity is an established practice among major central banks around the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clause 4 of the Bill will therefore lift current prohibitions in section 51(1) of the Act in a limited way by allowing approved financial institutions to pledge their security interests in residential property loans involving HDB flats as security to MAS in exchange for liquidity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In particular, this arrangement will neither affect flat owners' rights to their flats, nor result in any change to the terms and conditions of their housing loans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the period where the collateral is being pledged to MAS, HDB flat owners will continue to service their housing loans with the approved financial institution.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the highly unlikely scenario where an approved financial institution defaults on its loan from MAS, MAS will take over the residential property loans and HDB flat owners will be asked to re-direct their loan repayments to another approved financial institution appointed by MAS.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The terms and conditions of their housing loan will, for all purposes and intents, remain exactly the same.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, under the Housing and Development Act, HDB is empowered to compulsorily acquire flats if owners commit major infringements, such as unauthorised subletting.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Compulsory acquisition is a decision that is not taken lightly and is generally invoked only as a last resort or for very egregious infringements.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Unfortunately, such powers are necessary to allow HDB the ability to take commensurate action against the very small minority of flat owners who flout HDB's rules, and to safeguard our limited public housing supply for those who need it.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, the Act allows compulsory acquisition action to be taken against flat owners who deliberately make a misleading or false statement, or a misrepresentation of a material fact, in relation to their purchases of the flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clause 6 of the Bill will extend these powers to instances where the flat or an interest in it has been acquired from a related person, or an interest in the flat has been transferred to a related person.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will enable HDB to undertake compulsory acquisition if flat owners had intentionally made misleading or false statements, or misrepresented material facts in the transfer of flat ownership.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The incidence of such cases is very low.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Nevertheless, this will strengthen HDB's position to take compulsory acquisition action as a last resort should owners prove uncooperative and refuse to regularise the ownership of the flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The next amendment, set out in clause 5 of the Bill, is purely administrative.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, when a flat owner passes away and there is no surviving co-owner, family members who are eligible may apply to take over the ownership of the flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, there are situations where there is no one to take over the flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In such cases, HDB may step in and have the flat vested in HDB instead of leaving the flat vacant for a protracted period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, if there is no party to receive the compensation, or if there are disputes as to which parties it should be, HDB will apply to deposit the compensation with the Court where the compensation is held until there is a claim or the dispute is determined.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is to streamline the process for HDB and the Courts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There will not be any material change or impact on processes, other than a change in the judicial forum hearing HDB's applications for payments into Court.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Since HDB’s establishment in 1960, it has benefited from the strategic guidance of its Board in the performance of its statutory functions, and the development of plans and programmes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The diverse expertise of its Board members has also helped HDB to navigate challenges, and to develop as an organisation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The other Board-related amendments in clauses 2 and 3 are more administrative.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, they clarify that the Deputy Chairman position is a discretionary one and will only be appointed by the Minister when required.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, they will allow the Minister to temporarily appoint an acting Chairman, Deputy Chairman, or Member of the Board, in the event any of the individuals holding these positions is absent from duty or from Singapore.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Hopefully, it will provide another form of credit relief for businesses and individuals alike.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: With regard to the amendments made to section 6, 51(C) and 56, there are four areas of potential concerns and clarifications, I wish to seek from the Minister.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: First, the duration and effectiveness of this Facility.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Will this Facility be a temporary relief measure and if so, how long will this Facility last?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: On contrary, if the Facility will continue post-COVID as a permanent scheme, what are some of the benefits to the financial sector and will it be practiced in similar form as other jurisdictions, as the Minister mentioned earlier?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Second, the notification of homeowners on the banks pledging of the properties to MAS for the Facility.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: When the banks pledge the properties to MAS for loans, are the banks not required to inform the homeowners as part of the notification process even though it is an administrative procedure and I know it does not impact the existing service loan contract between the homeowner and the bank, but just as a notification process, is that still necessary?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: If homeowners are not informed, how would the following cases be handled?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: One, I think Minister has already touched in his briefing just now.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: For example, if the property is bequeathed under the Will to the homeowner's next of kin.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: In the unfortunate event when the mortgage is still outstanding and the homeowner is demised, then the beneficiary is below 21 years of age and is not of working age to be able to continue servicing the home loan, what are the implications to the property and the beneficiary?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I think the Minister touched upon how the property will not be compulsorily repossessed.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The second case I want to raise is there is an increasing trend of cross-marriages and in particular, across countries.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: So some of the homeowners have foreign spouses who are on LTVP or even LTVP+.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Some of them we know they are unlikely to be offered Permanent Residency whether it is due to age or other reasons.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: If the homeowner has passed on or is incarcerated, how will HDB address the situations where the foreign spouse only has LTVP, so they cannot effectively takeover ownership of the home, or for a spouse who is a foreigner but the couple has Singapore-born children?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: So, from the perspective of MAS, can the property continue to be pledged as collateral given the change in ownership?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The third area, this is in respect to the amendment on the Board Appointments.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: While I agree for HDB to have direct management of the Board Appointments to better support their plans and also their programmes, so that they are better oversight on their Statutory Board performance, I would like to understand two areas.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Would this expertise not be available if the right composition of Board members were judiciously selected to have the right diversity and provide the missing areas of expertise?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Are the current rules not sufficient to ensure that only eligible persons are able to purchase or retain the flats and properties?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: It is therefore of utmost importance that there is sound governance and proper oversight responsibility by the Board on matters relating to HDB, while also ensuring that public housing is not abused and remains affordable for those who need it the most.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: It is here that I would like to seek clarifications on two fronts, with regard to the proposed amendments to the Bill.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first is the amendment to section 6 of the HDB Act.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Based on my review of HDB's annual reports and the organisation structure of the Board enclosed within – the role of Deputy Chairman was not filled since Mr James Koh retired as Chairman on 30 September 2016 and was succeeded by Mr Bobby Chin who was the then Deputy Chairman.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I acknowledge, however, that from 1 October 2020 Prof Lily Kong will assume the role of Deputy Chairman for the new term of the HDB Board.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The current Act seems to require the Deputy Chairman role to be filled.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I would therefore like to clarify if any member of the Board has been serving as Deputy Chair from October 2016 to 30 September 2020.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I would also like to clarify what the reason the role was made discretionary and the initial intended role of the Deputy Chairman on the Board.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Who will be taking over that job scope should there be no Deputy Chairman appointed, once the amendments are passed?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In the event that the Chairman is absent from duty, how would the Minister decide on the member of the Board to act temporarily as Chairman?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The second amendment I would like to seek clarification on the proposed amendment to section 56.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: What was the reasoning for the inclusion of this amendment, and did it come from an observed trend on specific events and fact patterns, which the HDB has discovered when it comes specifically to related person transactions?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As compulsory acquisition is a harsh measure, I believe it is imperative for the Government to clarify further the rationale for the change.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This is especially so when clause 6 states that, "Flat owners who make misrepresentations whether innocently or otherwise, will be liable to have their flats acquired." Mdm Deputy Speaker, notwithstanding my clarifications on the amendments, I support the Housing and Development (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They help banks release funds into a tight economy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They penalise the use of falsehoods by HDB applicants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill allows banks to use HDB loans granted by them to obtain credit facilities and repurchase transactions from MAS.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This empowers MAS to inject more liquidity into our financial system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, MAS has recently created a new credit facility that allows certain banks to pledge home loans as collateral.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this crisis economy, homeowners will increasingly feel the brunt of unemployment and salary cuts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: More home loans will become delinquent or default.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MND itself said in 2018 that prolonged unemployment and drops in household income are two main reasons why households fall into mortgage arrears.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If households cannot repay their loans, banks will find it harder to repay MAS.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To clarify the significance of this amendment, I have two questions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, can Minister share data on what has been the default rate of HDB bank loans in the past five years?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, what is HDB's forecast of the default rate of HDB bank loans in the next 24 months?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is indeed a much needed lifeline for many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second clarification relates to falsehoods, transfers and acquisitions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This Bill gives HDB new powers to compulsorily acquire flats in certain cases.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have two sets of questions related to this proposal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One, in relation to both the existing section 56 and the new amendment, can Ministry clarify whether homeowners are allowed to amend the false or misleading statements in HDB applications they have submitted?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If so, what are the channels for them to amend their statements?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We must take a strong stance against the use of falsehoods in HDB applications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But where such falsehoods are assessed to be innocent or non-material, we should provide channels for voluntary correction.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Two, the amendment of section 56 introduces the terms "transfer" and "acquisition".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is no definition for either term in the Act for the purpose of section 56.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can Minister clarify what situations do "transfer" and "acquisition" refer to?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In particular, does the definition of "transfer" in section 56 differ from its definition in section 49, which expressly states to cover only section 49?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 56 has significant impact on lives, as it empowers HDB to compulsorily acquire flats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Clear definitions with examples, provided on Parliamentary record, will help avoid any doubt in its interpretation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My final point is that we have not gone far enough in reviewing our HDB policies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The policy of not allowing the keeping of cats in HDB flats has to be reviewed and changed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have spoken up about this for more than a decade now.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know this is not part of this Bill but I hope Minister will address this point.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When allowed to roam indiscriminately, they tend to shed fur and defecate or urinate in public areas and also make caterwauling sounds, which can inconvenience your neighbours.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It does not make sense that one is allowed to keep a dog and now a big dog, but not a cat, not even a little kitten.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Dogs can also shed fur and defecate or urinate in public areas.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We can ensure that pet cats do not roam indiscriminately and are sterilised.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have seen first-hand how all these simple measures can be taken and people can keep cats in their flats without affecting their neighbours." In response to my question, MND said, "When HDB receives a complaint, they go down and investigate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the cat is not causing any disamenities, the resident will not be asked to remove the cat".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate this reply but my question then is, what is the point of having a rule that we do not enforce?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So many people are already keeping cats in HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many of us, as Members of Parliament, see this during our home visits and some of us even take photos with our HDB residents and their cats.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We have worked from home, studied from home and our homes have sheltered us.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For some 3.2 million Singaporeans like me, that home is an HDB flat.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And for many Singaporeans who may face difficult times from the economic repercussions of this virus, holding on to our homes is one of our highest priorities.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I support the HDB's efforts and measures to help Singaporeans during this period.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am certain that this Bill on the Housing and Development Act will be of interest to many people who will want to know if they and their homes will be affected.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I also support the clear message from the Minister that the proposed amendments in this Bill will not impact HDB flat owners adversely.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I would like to raise some points.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our domestic banks can borrow from MAS as a lender of last resort, or for precautionary liquidity.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When they do so, these banks may have to offer some kind of assets as collateral or security for the loans.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Through this amendment, MAS will be able to recognise HDB residential mortgages placed with these banks as collateral and these banks will then be able to obtain more liquidity from MAS.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With this, banks can then extend a greater supply of credit to Singaporeans and Singaporean businesses.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is in line with efforts by MAS.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is critical for us to communicate to our fellow Singaporeans the impact of these changes, and make it clear if this amendment will affect HDB flat owners' rights.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We want to prevent the proliferation of false narratives.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We should also aim to provide clarity as to what would happen in the event that the collateral is enforced.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I appreciate that this would be an unusual situation, but given that we are living in unprecedented times, I believe Singaporeans want to be prepared for any outcome.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, in the event that MAS enforces on the HDB mortgages as collateral, will MAS, HDB or the bank provide prompt notice of the change to the affected HDB owner?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What administrative steps will HDB owners need to take in such a scenario?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They would likely have to change the bank they make their monthly mortgage payments to.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many of my residents are seniors, some of whom may not be technologically savvy or mobile, and unable to reproduce documents from a long time ago.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What is the process and timeline for the appointment of a replacement bank and how will mortgage payments be managed in the meantime?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What happens if some HDB owners accidentally continue to make mortgage payments to the former bank?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Second, when the HDB mortgage is administered by a replacement bank, will the commercial terms of the mortgage be kept the same vis-a-vis HDB owners?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is a fairly standard term in bank documentation that commercial banks may reserve the right to change the applicable interest rate without prior notice.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Needless to say, an increase in interest rates on the loans may have a hard financial impact on homeowners.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Third, aside from the effect of this amendment on HDB owners, I wish to ask the Minister whether this intended use of HDB mortgages as collateral, especially given the financially troubled times ahead, may lead to an increased pressure on the banks to foreclose on HDB mortgages with outstanding arrears more quickly in order to balance their books.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In other words, will Singaporeans who are unable to keep up with their loan installments be at greater risk of losing their homes?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I note that sections 56(1)(f) and (g), which are not amended, already allow the HDB to take CA action over a flat if an owner made a misleading statement or misrepresentation of a material fact relating to the purchase of that flat.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This amendment to introduce the new section 56(1)(ga) appears to extend the existing grounds in two ways.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: HDB can now take CA action against flat owners who had made a misleading statement or material misrepresentation.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One, in the transfer of a flat, and not just a purchase; and in relation to an owner's acquisition of an interest in the flat or the transfer of an interest in the flat to a related person, including a spouse, brother, parent or a remoter lineal ancestor or issue.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I note that this CA action right is intended to apply even if the person who made that misleading statement or misrepresentation about their eligibility to own the flat, did so innocently.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It seems a little harsh for HDB to take CA action over an innocent misrepresentation or misstatement, especially for eligibility factors which are straightforward or provable.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What are some examples of the misleading statements or misrepresentations relating to eligibility which prompted this amendment and why is it that these factors cannot be independently verified?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What factors will be taken into consideration in determining the compensation in the event of an innocent misrepresentation?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If the co-owners are not complicit and have done nothing wrong, it may come across as unfair to them to suffer the same severe consequences.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, will they be first given the opportunity to sell the flat on the open market?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I wish to state my appreciation for the difficult task that the Minister and HDB has in protecting and ensuring a fair outcome for HDB owners while ensuring that access to our HDB flats is not abused and used only by eligible persons as intended.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And I believe most Singaporeans do share that same appreciation.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Notwithstanding the above clarifications, I conclude my speech in support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Cheryl Chan asked if the MAS Singapore Dollar Term Facility is a temporary or permanent facility and if MAS can direct the banks to on-lend the funds borrowed from MAS to local businesses instead of chanelling them to overseas investments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: After the crisis is over, MAS will review if the facility needs to be retained.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The intent of the facility is not for the banks to directly on-lend the funds borrowed from MAS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Instead, the facility serves as a backstop that will provide banks with greater certainty of funding and provide the banks assurance and, in doing so, supports their lending to businesses and households during periods of heightened market uncertainty.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Cheryl Chan also asked if HDB flat owners will be notified when banks pledge their HDB loans to MAS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Nadia Samdin asked about the administrative implications on flat owners when MAS takes over the HDB loans and if the terms of HDB loans from banks will stay the same.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The borrower-lender relationship between the HDB flat owner and the bank, as set out in the terms and conditions of the housing loan, remains unchanged when the bank pledges the HDB loan to MAS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB flat owners continue to service their HDB loans with their respective banks and the bank still retains the legal title to the loan.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is, therefore, no change in the relationship between banks and the flat owners and, therefore, MAS will not require the bank to inform the HDB flat owners that their loans have been pledged to MAS as part of a portfolio of loans, both private and public, in return for this facility.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But in the highly unlikely scenario where a bank defaults on its loan from MAS, MAS will take ownership of the HDB loans and will appoint an agent bank to administer the loans on MAS' behalf.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under this scenario, HDB flat owners will be promptly notified to re-direct loan repayments to the agent bank.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is an administrative process and the terms and conditions of the HDB loans, including the interest rates charged, will not be affected in the process.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Again, we emphasise that this is a very unlikely scenario, as banks in Singapore are well capitalised and maintain healthy liquidity buffers and this is, indeed, a pre-emptive measure.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng shared his concerns that increased default rates on home loans during periods of economic uncertainty may increase the likelihood of banks defaulting on their loans from MAS and asked about the current and projected default rate of bank loans on HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The majority of borrowers are able to service their mortgages and should continue to avoid further build-up of debt.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But, we will keep a close watch on the situation as the crisis unfolds.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As Mr Ng has pointed out, economic and employment conditions remain challenging for many households, and we can expect homeowners to face difficulties in the period ahead.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This complements HDB's own loan arrangements which were announced a couple of days before MAS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Nadia Samdin also asked if the use of HDB loans as security will increase the pressure on banks to foreclose loans with outstanding arrears.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The MAS facility does not impact how banks manage their residential property loan portfolio.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As banks now have access to an added layer of liquidity insurance provided by MAS, their ability to deal with liquidity stress should in fact be enhanced.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In short, there is no impact on how such cases will be handled.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The existing HDB policies will continue to apply.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The banks will also continue to administer the loans based on their existing procedures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have sought to respond to Members’ queries regarding the amendments made to enable the MAS SGD Term Facility.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If there are further technical queries relating to this or to the financial system, my colleague Minister Ong Ye Kung will be here to address them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Next, let me address the points made regarding compulsory acquisition.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Nadia Samdin asked if this would excessively penalise flat owners who may be innocent and unaware of the false statements or misrepresentation of facts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Before initiating acquisition action, HDB will investigate each case thoroughly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Depending on the circumstances of each case, HDB may instead consider imposing a financial penalty or issue a warning.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB will consider the interest of the parties involved, including any non-complicit owners and occupiers of the flat, and may allow the flat to be sold on the open market if there are extenuating circumstances.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The statutory appeal channel to the Minister under section 56 of the Act serves as yet an additional safeguard to the interests of potentially non-complicit owners.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Chua asked about the rationale for this amendment and, like Miss Cheryl Chan, also asked if there had been a significant rise in false statements or misrepresentations in the transfer of flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: By and large, HDB's existing process and system checks are able to reduce such occurrences.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about avenues for owners to amend unintentional or non-material errors in their applications to HDB.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: He asked also about the specific definitions of the terms “acquisition” and “transfer” in the amendment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member is right that the definition of the term "transfer" in section 49 applies expressly to that section only.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Section 49 sets out the various transactions for which HDB may act for parties who do not engage their own solicitors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Such transactions include, among others, the purchase, sale, transfer of ownership interest, and surrender of HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The definition of "transfer" in section 49 is therefore purposefully broad, to cover the range of transactions where HDB can act for, some of which do not apply to the intended amendment in section 56.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To explain, the term "acquisition" in this amendment refers to the obtaining of an interest in the ownership of the flat by an incoming owner.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The term “transfer” here refers to an interest in the ownership of the flat being passed to an incoming owner.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When a couple includes their child as a co-owner of a flat, the child acquires an interest in the flat, while the parents transfer an interest in the flat to the child.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I mentioned earlier, the HDB Board plays a strategic role in guiding the development of the Board.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When appointing Board members, we seek a diverse representation of perspectives to cover the breadth of its work.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, with the current Board size, HDB has had to make trade-offs in selecting and bringing on expertise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the Member’s question as to whether HDB had considered enlisting the help of external consultants or industry experts instead, I would like to share that HDB does, indeed, engage such experts when dealing with specific projects or issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, HDB has several advisory panels comprising industry experts to guide HDB in technical areas such as Architecture, Research, and Civil and Structural Engineering.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Such panels are useful when HDB needs advice in more specific and technical areas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But they will not be able to replace the Board’s role in offering strategic guidance and contributing diverse viewpoints, including beyond their core areas of expertise, to guide HDB’s overall development.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Chua had asked about the appointment of a Deputy Chairman prior to the appointment of Dr Lily Kong as Deputy Chairman with effect October 2020.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Prior to appointment, at the start of each term of HDB's Board, there would be appointed in HDB's Board a temporary chairman who would for all purposes and intents perform the role of a Deputy Chairman in managing the Board and holding Board meetings in the absence of the Chairman.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This amendment brings the structure and composition of the HDB's Board in line with other Boards such as JTC, URA and LTA.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This Bill relates to credit, compulsory acquisition, courts and candidates for the Board – four Cs – and that does not include the cats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nevertheless, let me address Mr Louis Ng's point about the need to review HDB’s policy that disallows the keeping of cats in HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB’s pet ownership policies seek to strike a balance between residents who are pet lovers and those who are not.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continually review and I assure the Member that we will review and update our pet ownership policies to ensure that they are effective and balance the needs of different stakeholders.
